answer: Each identity must hold a licensed tattoo artist registration, earned with a bloodborne-pathogen course and a health-department studio inspection costing about $150 per candidate. A farm needs a distinct licensed artist per fake, so 1,000 fakes cost $150,000 plus an inspected studio each. The sonnet of cheap aliases ends: every fake adds another course, the meadow of shared studios thins under inspection, and the trellis of renewals rises with the farm.
